explainedBy: A refute diagram dismantles the myth that allowing anger somatic energy means endorsing angry cognitive thoughts.

storyboard.claim: Saying yes to bodily anger is not validating the narrative of angry thoughts.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A refute diagram contrasting physical sensation against cognitive narrative, stamping out thought endorsement.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the previous question of whether allowing anger acts as a permission slip.
storyboard.addedInformation: Explicitly separates bodily sensation from cognitive narrative in the diagram structure.

explainedBy: Roger rages in the office as the cognitive narrative spins stories that colleagues are idiots disrespecting him.

storyboard.claim: Cognitive content is the mental narrative spinning accusations that others are disrespectful.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Roger in the office, teeth gritted in anger, gesturing forcefully as he talks.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Exemplifies the cognitive narrative side broken down from the previous distinction.
storyboard.addedInformation: Grounds the abstract concept of cognitive content in Roger corporate frustration.

explainedBy: A flow diagram maps energetic reality directly to measurable physiological activation like a 120 bpm heart rate.

storyboard.claim: Energetic reality is physical sensation rather than intellectual justification.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow diagram connecting a 120 bpm racing heartbeat directly to somatic reality.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts from the cognitive narrative to its physiological counterpart: the bodily sensation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Isolates the biological metric of rapid heartbeat without emotional interpretation.

explainedBy: Roger sits slumped with clenched jaw and sweating palms, radically accepting his internal storm.

storyboard.claim: Accepting bodily sensations means acknowledging the internal weather without agreeing with the mental story.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Roger sitting in his room looking worried and slumped beside a storm icon, holding his tense posture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Synthesizes physical sensations into the metaphor of an internal weather system.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Roger ceasing outward fight while visibly experiencing intense physiological strain.

explainedBy: Roger stays present with the storm inside his nervous system without acting out the destructive strikes.

storyboard.claim: You accept the internal thunderstorm without endorsing or acting on destructive impulses.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Roger in the same bedroom setting with the storm icon, his tense expression relaxing to neutral stillness.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the internal storm stage from beat 123 while shifting Roger posture from strain to non-reactivity.
storyboard.addedInformation: Demonstrates the exact somatic shift from being gripped by anger to resting as the conscious observer.

explainedBy: Tara explains that while resistance feeds destructive fire, allowing starves the emotional flame of oxygen.

storyboard.claim: Resistance fuels the fire of reactivity while allowing starves it of fuel.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tara framed close-up beside a burning fire icon, calmly explaining the mechanism of non-resistance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reveals the underlying dynamic: fighting feelings intensifies them, allowing dissolves them.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pairs Tara authoritative calm with the literal fire motif being depowered.

explainedBy: Mitch stands quietly on the shore in the rain instead of screaming fruitlessly at the stormy sky.

storyboard.claim: Allowing means accepting the storm is falling instead of screaming at the sky.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mitch standing calmly on the shore beside water under an open sky, experiencing the rain without fighting it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Translates the psychological principle into the concrete metaphor of standing peacefully in the rain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visualizes peaceful acceptance amidst elemental turbulence on an expansive shore.

explainedBy: Mitch breaks the cycle of struggle by ceasing to battle the internal prison warden on his own turf.

storyboard.claim: Allowing stops empowering the internal prison warden through endless resistance.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mitch stands steady in a quiet room as heavy chains snap apart, refusing combat with his inner warden.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Deepens the metaphor from weather acceptance to disarming the punitive internal critic.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the release of resistance visually manifested as breaking chains.

explainedBy: Mitch experiences deep biological relief as adrenaline subsides and clear stillness returns.

storyboard.claim: Once resistance stops, adrenaline clears and nervous system equilibrium returns.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mitch in the same room, his face relaxing into calm relief as inner stillness settles.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues Mitch in the room post-chain release, capturing the physical aftermath of calming adrenaline.
storyboard.addedInformation: Portrays the restorative calm following the cessation of somatic fight-or-flight.

explainedBy: A flow diagram shows how opening space enables examining the core drivers beneath the storm.

storyboard.claim: Space must lead to investigating what generated the storm or the pattern will return.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow diagram linking the open calm space directly to looking at the deep driver beneath the storm.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transitions from momentary calm to the necessity of structural inquiry.
storyboard.addedInformation: Charts the operational link between creating emotional space and probing root causes.

explainedBy: A sorter diagram contrasts the second step of Allowing with the third step of Investigate with care.

storyboard.claim: The practice shifts from passive allowing to active inquiry in the investigate step.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sorter diagram sorting the protocol from passive allowing into active inquiry.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Formally delineates the shift from the A step to the I step in RAIN.
storyboard.addedInformation: Categorizes the methodological transition from non-resistance to somatic investigation.

explainedBy: Mitch sits tightly in a therapist chair, jaw muscles visibly bulging in concentrated strain.

storyboard.claim: A client sits in the therapy office with jaw muscles clenched tight in intense concentration.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mitch seated in a clinical armchair, face clenched tight with strain and worry.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces a clinical case study illustrating the physical intensity of investigation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pins the psychological inquiry to physical tension in the seated body.

explainedBy: Mitch sits agonizing over his ex-partner beside an aching heart icon.

storyboard.claim: He is painfully gripped by toxic obsession over wanting his partner back.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mitch remains seated in the therapy office, staring forward with anguish beside a heart icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the clinical office session, detailing the romantic fixation driving his somatic strain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Connects his physical clenching directly to romantic obsession and emotional agony.

explainedBy: Guided to investigate bodily sensation, Mitch pauses analytical reflection about childhood.

storyboard.claim: When asked where desire lives, he does not offer a psychological dissection of childhood.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mitch seated in the chair, pausing intellectual analysis and turning attention inward.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts psychological intellectualization with true somatic location.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the pivot away from mental storytelling toward bodily awareness.

explainedBy: Mitch grips his chest with both hands describing a sharp claw tearing into his heart.

storyboard.claim: He describes a clawed hand violently ripping and shredding his actual chest tissue.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mitch seated in the therapist office, hands clutched over his chest in pain beside a crack icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reveals the raw somatic imagery David/Mitch encounters upon investigating his chest.
storyboard.addedInformation: Conveys the visceral, violent imagery of emotional pain in the physical body.

explainedBy: A refute diagram dismantles the idea that investigation means figuring out childhood blame from 20 years ago.

storyboard.claim: Investigation is not analytical dissection or figuring out past parental faults.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A refute diagram rejecting intellectual childhood analysis in favor of direct somatic investigation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Clarifies the core nature of somatic investigation versus mental theorizing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Separates psychological theorizing from felt somatic inquiry using the refute structure.

explainedBy: Roger hides behind an intellectual mask because analyzing keeps him safely detached from the body.

storyboard.claim: The brain loves intellectual analysis because it keeps you safely disconnected from bodily pain.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Roger in a room gesturing intellectually beside a mask icon, smugly rationalizing feelings.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the ego defensive motive behind compulsive over-analysis.
storyboard.addedInformation: Uses the mask icon to portray intellectualizing as an evasive ego defense.

explainedBy: A flow diagram defines true investigation as somatic curiosity tracking emotion in bodily tissue.

storyboard.claim: True investigation is somatic curiosity locating exactly where emotion lives in physical tissue.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow diagram linking open somatic curiosity directly to feeling emotion in living tissue.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Replaces the rejected analytical mode with genuine somatic curiosity.
storyboard.addedInformation: Maps somatic inquiry directly into bodily geography.

explainedBy: A sorter diagram categorizes the primary physical sensations interrogated to identify unmet needs.

storyboard.claim: Interrogating physical sensations like tight throat, hollow stomach, or racing pulse uncovers unmet needs.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sorter diagram breaking somatic cues into tight throat, hollow pit, and racing pulse.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Catalogs the specific somatic checkpoints checked during investigation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Organizes bodily sensations into distinct diagnostic channels.

explainedBy: A causal diagram illustrates using the physical body as an internal radar discovering emotional wounds.

storyboard.claim: The physical body functions like a radar system detecting deep psychological wounds.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A causal chain showing bodily sensation traveling through sensory radar into the core psychological wound.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Models the sensory radar concept that bridges somatic feedback with emotional roots.
storyboard.addedInformation: Traces the pathway from raw physical feeling to revealed psychological injury.

explainedBy: Janice sits holding her hand tightly to her chest, investigating dark, heavy, squeezing panic.

storyboard.claim: A young woman touches her chest, feeling dark, heavy, tight squeezing during inquiry.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Janice seated in a quiet room, one hand placed tenderly over her chest with a worried expression.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces Sophia/Janice clinical inquiry into sudden breakup panic.
storyboard.addedInformation: Grounds the somatic investigation in a gentle, direct physical touch to the chest.

explainedBy: Breathing into the tightness, Janice sees a vision of a frightened little girl feeling fundamentally flawed.

storyboard.claim: Staying with the sensation reveals an image of a terrified younger self believing she is unlovable.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Janice in the same room beside a mirror icon, looking sad as she connects with her wounded child within.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the somatic inquiry until the physical sensation yields its underlying visual memory.
storyboard.addedInformation: Uses the mirror icon to represent meeting the internal reflection of her vulnerable child.

explainedBy: A flow diagram contrasts the superficial breakup narrative with the deep somatic truth of terror.

storyboard.claim: She moved from the cognitive surface story of a breakup down into the somatic truth of feeling unlovable.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow diagram moving from the cognitive surface breakup story into the deep somatic truth.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarizes the trajectory from external event to primal emotional vulnerability.
storyboard.addedInformation: Diagrams the descent from conceptual complaint to core somatic vulnerability.

explainedBy: Tara holds a key explaining that true somatic investigation unlocks the ego defenses to reveal the real wound.

storyboard.claim: True investigation bypasses ego excuses and reveals the actual wound.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tara holding a key in a calm room, serenely gesturing as she describes unlocking deep healing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Affirms the core breakthrough of the Investigation step in the RAIN practice.
storyboard.addedInformation: Uses the key prop to symbolize unlocking access beneath the defenses of the ego.

explainedBy: Mitch expresses serious concern that diving directly into intense visceral trauma sounds terrifying.

storyboard.claim: Diving straight into visceral agony sounds terrifying and raises a major clinical concern.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mitch in the room, looking worried and raising his hands as he voices deep reservations.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the critical counter-question regarding safety and trauma risks.
storyboard.addedInformation: Captures the genuine fear of emotional overwhelm that practitioners often face.

explainedBy: Roger slumps in fear beside a crack icon, terrified that looking at intense pain will make him lose his grip.

storyboard.claim: What happens if trauma is overwhelming and looking at it causes someone to lose control?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Roger slumped in fear beside a crack icon in his bedroom, gripped by the fear of emotional collapse.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Intensifies the safety concern into the personal dread of psychological disintegration.
storyboard.addedInformation: Emphasizes the intense dread of losing cognitive and emotional stability.

explainedBy: A speaker confronts the severe danger of medical retraumatization for individuals suffering from PTSD.

storyboard.claim: Does forcing inquiry into intense trauma risk severely retraumatizing patients with PTSD?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A close-up of a worried face in a clinical setting questioning medical retraumatization risks.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Frames the personal fear of overwhelm as a recognized clinical PTSD danger.
storyboard.addedInformation: Directly addresses clinical psychiatric risk with striking text.

explainedBy: Tara introduces Dr. Dan Siegel foundational concept of the window of tolerance for safe trauma navigation.

storyboard.claim: Clinical practice must responsibly address trauma through Dr. Dan Siegel window of tolerance.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tara speaking calmly and authoritatively in a meditation room introducing the window of tolerance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the danger objection by introducing the clinical framework for emotional capacity.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes Tara clinical authority and provides theoretical safety bounds.

explainedBy: A spectrum diagram illustrates the optimal middle bandwidth where difficult emotions are processed safely.

storyboard.claim: The window of tolerance is a bandwidth where emotions can be processed while staying grounded.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A spectrum diagram showing the balanced central zone between hypoarousal and hyperarousal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Visually diagrams the window of tolerance framework introduced in the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Plots the optimal therapeutic bandwidth between opposite pathological extremes.

explainedBy: The spectrum marker pushes high into hyperarousal when fear exceeds the safe therapeutic window.

storyboard.claim: If fear pushes a person outside the window into hyperarousal, the nervous system becomes overwhelmed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The spectrum diagram continues with the marker spiked high into the dangerous hyperarousal zone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the spectrum diagram, moving the indicator into hyperarousal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tracks the exact moment inquiry breaches biological regulation limits.

explainedBy: A causal loop diagram shows how overwhelming panic traps the brain into repeating traumatic flashbacks.

storyboard.claim: Hyperarousal causes somatic investigation to backfire, locking the brain into a repetitive trauma loop.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A causal loop diagram illustrating how overwhelm and panic circle endlessly back into the trauma loop.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the neurological mechanism behind why pushing through panic fails.
storyboard.addedInformation: Demonstrates how exceeding tolerance reinforces rather than heals traumatic cycles.

explainedBy: A flow diagram charts the emergency clinical protocol: abort the investigation immediately upon hitting overwhelm.

storyboard.claim: If you exceed your window of tolerance, you must immediately abort investigation and restore safety.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow diagram directing immediate cessation of inquiry and direct transition to safety.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Presents the clear, decisive safety instruction counteracting hyperarousal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Establishes a firm medical rule against pushing past traumatic thresholds.

explainedBy: Tara holds a protective shield demonstrating jumping immediately to the Nurture step for baseline safety.

storyboard.claim: Abandon the investigation and jump straight to nurturing to reestablish biological safety.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tara holding a shield in a calm room, illustrating protective self-nurturing over forced endurance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Details the exact emergency action step: jumping directly to Nurture.
storyboard.addedInformation: Uses the shield prop to symbolize immediate self-protection and soothing.

explainedBy: Tara emphasizes that one must never force oneself to stare into an abyss if actively destabilizing.

storyboard.claim: Do not force yourself to stare into the abyss if your nervous system is actively dysregulated.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tara continuing in the room, gesturing firmly against heroic self-endurance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reinforces the protective directive against dangerous stoic perseverance.
storyboard.addedInformation: Stands against the harmful myth that trauma therapy requires agonizing suffering.

explainedBy: Staying grounded inside the window, Mitch accurately maps the physical bars constructed in his body.

storyboard.claim: Staying in the window maps the exact physical bars the prison warden has built inside your tissue.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mitch standing calmly in the room beside intact chains, clearly discerning the physical boundaries of his tension.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to successful investigation when staying within safe regulatory bounds.
storyboard.addedInformation: Connects the chains motif back to the somatic architecture of emotional defense.

explainedBy: Framed in close-up, Mitch finally sees the internal cage clearly without fear or denial.

storyboard.claim: You finally see the cage for exactly what it is and where it lives in your physical body.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mitch framed close up beside the chains, observing his bodily confinement with lucid clarity.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the somatic mapping sequence by achieving complete lucidity about the inner trap.
storyboard.addedInformation: Highlights conscious clarity dissolving unconscious identification with the prison.

explainedBy: A flow diagram transitions from mapping somatic pain to the active protocol of healing.

storyboard.claim: This marks the turning point transitioning from observing pain to actively healing it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow diagram connecting the observation of pain directly into active healing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Bridges the analytical phase of Investigate to the transformational phase of Nurture.
storyboard.addedInformation: Summarizes the pivotal paradigm shift at the heart of the RAIN practice.

explainedBy: Brenda rests peacefully in retreat attire beside a glowing heart icon, initiating Nurture with loving presence.

storyboard.claim: Nurture with loving presence represents the active turning point where healing begins.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Brenda standing centered and warm in the meditation room beside a radiant heart icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Launches the final and most transformative step: Nurture with loving presence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Embodies loving presence and compassion in Brenda centered demeanor.
